Bug_Explanation: This is an unnecessary object creation of String class. Instead of using new String(), we can directly assign the string to the object. This is because String is an immutable class in Java and can be safely shared. Thus, this operation can lead to unnecessary memory usage and potential performance issues.
Trigger_Explanation: This JUNIT test case triggers the bug by invoking the method showBug of the class StringInstantiation. The showBug method is trying to print a String object 'bar' which is created using the new String constructor. This constructor is unnecessary as Strings in Java are immutable and can be safely shared. Thus, the String object 'bar' is created each time showBug is called, which can lead to unnecessary memory usage and potential performance issues.
